summary: I applied the builder's maths patch to a fresh worktree at e4ce22b. The registry hunk no longer applied, so I left it out and regenerated docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json in a copy (4 operations added, record_registry --check shows no differences). I fixed both must-fix findings and all eleven should-fix items. (1) Kasandra's plans: stacy_control.validate_actions now reads every string inside a provider command's arguments, at any depth, as a possible maths line. It reads them as route_program and compile_program do: zero-width spaces removed, a leading 'explain' dropped. So investigation.step, investigation.check, agenda.add, agenda.suggest, stac.* and any later command that carries a line with 'given' are refused, with the owner-worded constant GIVEN_IS_THE_OWNERS. (2) A check over a sound or widened range now says 'at least X to spare', 'over by at least X' or 'short by at least X', rounded down, and gives the reason (the margin may be wider than the true one). When it cannot tell, it says it 'cannot be told from this range' and no longer says 'the ranges reach both sides'. Exact (ATTAINED) ranges keep both ends. Should-fix: refusals are in the owner's words, with no codes, node ids or 'Cannot ge'. Allowed ends and whole-step ends are rounded inward and the step past them outward. An equation's end is said once and exactly. EXACT_ALLOWED_SET is claimed only when an end was worked out again; otherwise the receipt says no guarantee is claimed. A number that is too long is refused as too long. An integer quantity's range must have whole-number ends. A 'given' on the solved quantity and 'for' outside solve are refused, not dropped. Implementation hashes are taken once, at import. stac.status now gives math_grammar. The docs page explains the sheet ID and how to set a tolerance. A new test guards the Terminal and Kasandra receipt links. Results: test_math_core has 33 tests and test_math_lines 13, all passing in both looks. The 73-module tier-1 list passes in both looks: 1186 tests in each, no failures, errors or skips. I showed that every new test fails on the builder's code. I retook the solve frames in both looks at 1366x768 and read them. Patch: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Struthio/62270cd8-8155-590e-b29e-91307882a142/scratchpad/work/b085/maths.patch (143528 bytes, 16 files). It applies to a clean archive of HEAD.

decisions: The planner guard reads every string in a provider command's arguments, at any depth, as a possible maths line, not only a 'program' argument of named commands. Reason: it covers the four carriers the review found and any later command that keeps or runs a line, with no list to keep current. A string that is a whole maths line with a 'given' is refused wherever it sits, which errs on the safe side.
gives_ranges reads a line as route_program does (zero-width spaces removed, a leading 'explain' in any case dropped, first word 'math'), so a line cannot slip through by its spelling.

The planner's refusal is the constant stacy_control.GIVEN_IS_THE_OWNERS, worded for the owner: 'A range in a maths line is given by the owner, never proposed: a tolerance the owner sets is used instead'. Tests compare against the constant, not the wording.

Over a sound or widened range, a check gives only the near end of the margin as 'at least X', rounded down, and says why. That near end is the only true bound; the far end may be loose. An exact (ATTAINED) range keeps both ends.

When solving an equation (==), its one end is shown in its exact value, a decimal when exact and a fraction otherwise, because no rounded figure of a single allowed point holds. The main words say 'Exactly 1/3'.
When no end was worked out again, the guarantee is None and the receipt says 'Guarantee: none claimed'. I did not invent a new guarantee name, because the design names four.

Refusals: each state has its own owner sentence. It is used when the reason carries a code, a node id or a solver term, and always for DIMENSION_MISMATCH. Three reasons are reworded specifically (zero denominator, negative power of zero, unknown unit). The record's 'reason' field keeps the technical text; only the words on screen change.
An integer quantity's range with fractional ends is refused (DOMAIN_ERROR), not snapped inward. The owner typed that range, and changing it quietly would be another silent fallback.
Implementation hashes are taken once at import (math_answers.IMPLEMENTATION), so they record the code actually loaded.
I regenerated the registry against e4ce22b in the copy and copied the file back, so the whole patch applies to current main.
The docs say to set a tolerance with /tolerances.set in the Terminal (/help tolerances.set lists its arguments) or by asking Kasandra, and that the window has no control of its own for it yet.

The FOCUSED_MODULES entry for test_math_core and test_math_lines in tools/check_hatch.py is unchanged from the builder: on its own line, with blank lines around it, away from the other builders' lines.

release_note: Maths in lines: a maths line on a problem sheet can now solve for a quantity, give the range of an expression, or check a limit, worked out in exact fractions. Each answer says Holds, Does not hold or Cannot tell. Numbers are rounded the safe way with the exact value beside them, and one word away is the receipt: the inputs with their revisions, the method and the guarantee. Ranges come only from you, typed in the line or set as a tolerance; Kasandra never writes one, and she always asks before she sets a tolerance. When a range can only be bounded loosely, the answer says 'at least' and why, instead of claiming more than is known.
